capabilities.name: Wall / Door / Window / Column / Slab instance recovery from Revit 2024 partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records + partition_schema_mvp::instances_from_partition_category_records / slabs_from_partition_category_records + partition_ifc_export_overrides; tests/project_count_fixtures.rs (IFCWALL 360/360, IFCDOOR 132/132, IFCWINDOW 6/6, IFCCOLUMN 256/256, IFCSLAB 80/80, IFCSHADINGDEVICE 20/20, tolerance 0) and the magnetar-2024-core-interior-slim OctetProof verdict, where entity_counts.IFCWALL / IFCDOOR / IFCWINDOW / IFCCOLUMN / IFCSLAB / IFCSHADINGDEVICE are all inside the claimed surface and rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell and IFClite agree exactly
capabilities.notes: Scope is six BuiltInCategories (OST_Walls, OST_Doors, OST_Windows, OST_Columns, OST_Floors, OST_BuildingPad), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. Selection is a direct byte test, not a heuristic: the record must carry no container reference at +0x32 and placement kind 0xffffef7f at +0x42 (RE-21). It supersedes the #204 column rule, whose family-local bbox proxy and highest-ElementId-per-footprint collapse are removed. RE-22 (#212) extended the same rule to slabs and found it already exact there: its 99 OST_Floors selections are all exported (79 IfcSlab + 20 IfcShadingDevice), and the 80th exported slab is an OST_BuildingPad (Pad:Site Pad, ElementId 21975). The IfcSlab / IfcShadingDevice split is a per-instance Revit 'IFC Export As' override read out of the partition parameter block: the UTF-16LE value string with the owning ElementId as a u64 at -0x0dc and again at -0x11e, both required to agree and to be declared in Global/ElemTable. Thirty-one entries pass on this file, naming 21 ids; the 20 that are also placed instances are exactly the export's IFCSHADINGDEVICE Tag set. Only IfcShadingDevice is honoured as an override target — an unrecognised value leaves the element on its class mapping. Where one ElementId is framed more than once, the record with the greatest bounding-box z extent is kept; that agrees with the export's IfcExtrudedAreaSolid.Depth on 79 of 80 slabs (the 80th is exported as two stacked solids summing to it). Ties go to the newest frame - the greatest (stream, offset) - because Revit rewrites an edited element into a higher-numbered Partitions stream and leaves the earlier copy in place (RE-26): 171 of 360 walls and 96 of 132 doors carry two frames that disagree about the plan box, and on the newest one the wall's thin plan extent equals the nominal thickness of the IfcWallType Revit's export assigns on 360 of 360 (201 of 360 on the oldest) and its type slot equals that IfcWallType.Tag on 356 of 360 (183 of 360 on the oldest; the positional read is superseded by RE-28's set test, which is 360 of 360 - see element-record-wall-type-join). Global/ElemTable's u32 at +0x1c is a monotone version counter that ranks the same way across all 976 exported instances. No frame of any instance on this file disagrees about the box's z, so the tie-break cannot move an element between storeys - storey_bound_elements was 801 either way when this was measured, and is 853 since #219 / RE-27. Column, window, slab and building-pad boxes are unchanged; door boxes move without a measurement that adjudicates them, since a door's record box is not the panel Revit exports and 0 of 132 are world-exact either way. Bodies are the record's own bounding box, not a recovered family profile or wall location curve; for plates the z extent is the real thickness, and since RE-25 (#31) the plan profile of a slab whose sketch closes is the recovered sketch boundary rather than the box rectangle - see element-record-slab-plan-profile. Base/top Level ElementIds stay unbound (#86); doors and windows are attached to their host wall as of RE-23/#222 (see element-record-door-window-host-binding). Storey containment came from the #213 column-derived elevation set when this row landed: walls, doors and columns bound by their record base, plates by their record top face (Revit hangs a floor below its level) — 51 of 100 plates bound and all 51 agreed with the export, none wrongly, while windows never bound because their record base is a sill height, measured 0 of 6. Since #219 / RE-27 the first join tried is the Level ElementId the record itself names, which reaches all 100 plates and all 6 windows; that elevation path survives as the fallback - see record-level-reference-storey-bind. This is not evidence for any other category or release.
capabilities.user_impact: Walls, doors, windows, architectural columns, floor slabs and building pads come out of a Revit 2024 project as placed IFC entities with position, a solid body and (for slabs) a measured thickness and plan profile, matching Revit's own export element for element.

capabilities.name: Door and Window host-wall binding from Revit 2024 partition element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::decode_reference_list + partition_schema_mvp::opening_instances_from_records; tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_door_window_host_wall_binding compares the emitted (host wall, opening) pairs against the reference export's own IfcRelVoidsElement + IfcRelFillsElement chain and requires exact set equality (138/138, 0 wrong, 0 missing); the magnetar-2024-core-interior-slim OctetProof verdict carries relations.IFCRELFILLSELEMENT inside the claimed surface, where rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell 0.8.5 and IFClite 7.1.1 emit byte-identical 138-pair sets
capabilities.notes: Scope is two BuiltInCategories (OST_Doors, OST_Windows), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. The carrier is a counted reference list that follows the element record's bounding box: a u32 length at +0x88 and that many u64 slots at +0x8c. The host is the slot immediately before the record's own ElementId, accepted only when it is one of the 360 ElementIds the RE-21 instance rule selects as exported walls, so a wrong read fails closed instead of inventing a host. Measured on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt: 273 of 273 door/window records give the correct host, and the emitted IfcRelFillsElement pair set equals Revit's own exactly - 138 of 138, no wrong host, no missing pair, no extra pair. Three fixed-shape readings were rejected and are recorded in RE-23: u64 at +0xac is right on 186 of 273 records, u64 at +0xa4 on 81, and 'the last two slots are (host, self)' on 192 - the list length varies (6 on every door record, 18 on every window record, up to 101 elsewhere) and 81 door records continue past their own id with a trailing type-symbol slot. The predecessor read is not a category discriminator: 528 of 638 wall records also have a wall predecessor, which is why the rule is applied only to the two categories RE-21 already identifies by BuiltInCategory. Emission is the IFC4 chain Revit uses - IfcOpeningElement (bodied with the door/window's own record bounding box, placed on the element's placement, not a wall-relative cut) plus IfcRelVoidsElement and IfcRelFillsElement. The opening's Tag repeats the filling element's, which is what the reference export does on all 138. The export's other 63 IfcOpeningElement - 42 in slabs, 20 in shading devices, 1 unfilled wall penetration - are not recovered: rvt-rs emits no opening that is not filled by a recovered element. This is not evidence for any other category or release.
capabilities.user_impact: Doors and windows come out of a Revit 2024 project as IFC4 fills of a real host wall, so a viewer subtracts the opening from the wall and shows the door in it - matching Revit's own export relationship for relationship.

capabilities.name: Slab plan profile from Revit 2024 OST_SketchLines element records
capabilities.evidence: element_record_plan_profiles::plan_profiles_from_sketch_line_records wired through partition_schema_mvp::slabs_from_partition_category_records; reports/element-framing/RE-25-slab-plan-profiles.md; gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_slab_plan_profiles (80 of 100 record-backed plates resolve a profile, and the 20 that do not are exactly the export's IFCSHADINGDEVICE Tag set) plus the unit gates in src/element_record_plan_profiles.rs
capabilities.user_impact: A Revit 2024 floor slab exports with the polygon its sketch actually encloses - including its voids - instead of the bounding rectangle, so a courtyard ring comes out as a ring.
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_SketchLines, -2000045), one release band (Revit 2024), one recorded edge, and only the plates the RE-22 instance rule already recovers. The join is exact and byte-anchored: the last slot of the second counted reference list at +0x88 names the sketched element, and the 3688 sketch-line records on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt name 126 owners including all 80 exported IFCSLAB and all 20 exported IFCSHADINGDEVICE ids. No geometry takes part in the join. The reconstruction is a closure rule over the recorded segment bounding boxes, not a fit: a box degenerate on one axis contributes its endpoints, every other box is placed only when exactly one pair of still-open vertices fits it, and an ambiguous segment, a vertex that does not finish at degree 2, an unused edge, a zero-extent box or a loop under three vertices rejects the whole element. Measured against Revit's own export (IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, project plan frame, cyclic sequences with orientation normalised, tolerance 1e-3 ft per vertex): 80 of 80 slab profiles exact across 122 loops - 80 outer plus 42 rectangular voids - worst vertex deviation 1.563e-12 ft, and 2.842e-14 ft re-measured on the emitted IFC after the metre round-trip. 42 perimeter plates emit IFCARBITRARYPROFILEDEFWITHVOIDS (26-vertex outer ring, one rectangular void) and 38 emit IFCARBITRARYCLOSEDPROFILEDEF. Status is partial rather than verified because that agreement is measured and regression-gated but is not a field of either OctetProof claimed surface: no witness compares profile geometry, so this has not met the two-independent-witnesses bar in docs/verification-protocol.md. The 20 exported IFCSHADINGDEVICE are rotated plates whose 57 sketch-line boxes include one of zero extent and 21 diagonals with no axis-parallel anchor; the closure declines all 20 and they keep the record box rectangle with ProfileResolved false. The pre-RE-25 plan-loop scan is a measured dead end here: 2317 closed plan-polyline candidates across all eight inflated partitions, none with the plan bounds of any recovered plate, and no ordered vertex run of the export's polygon anywhere in the file at any stride. Walls, doors, windows and columns still carry the record bounding box; base/top Level ElementId binding stays open (#86). This is not evidence for any other category or release.

capabilities.name: Wall body from Revit 2024 element records: run cut back by the joins the record names, plus thin-axis thickness
capabilities.evidence: element_record_wall_joins::joined_walls and ::join_trims wired through partition_schema_mvp::wall_instances_from_records; reports/element-framing/RE-26-world-coordinate-residuals.md and reports/element-framing/RE-29-join-reference-list.md; gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_wall_join_trimmed_bodies (360 of 360 walls resolve, 322 take a trim), ::core_interior_2024_wall_joins_are_named_in_the_reference_list, the unit gates in src/element_record_wall_joins.rs including the_surviving_side_of_a_true_l_corner_is_still_over_trimmed, and the pinned ObjectPlacement x Position composition of wall 20800 in tools/ci/ifc_schema_arity.py
capabilities.user_impact: A Revit 2024 wall exports at the length its joins actually leave it, with the wall's real thickness, instead of the untrimmed centreline-to-centreline box - and the join partners are read out of the file rather than inferred from geometry alone.
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Walls, -2000011), one release band (Revit 2024), one recorded edge, and only axis-parallel walls - every wall on this file is axis-parallel, and a box with no distinguishable thin plan axis is declined. Three measured facts back it. First, the box's thin plan extent is the wall's thickness: on the newest frame of each element it equals the nominal thickness of the IfcWallType Revit's export assigns on 360 of 360 walls. Second, every non-zero delta between the box and Revit's Axis polyline over all 720 wall ends is exactly 0.25, 0.3333 or 0.75 ft - half of the 6-inch, 8-inch and 18-inch wall thicknesses on the file - and zero everywhere else, so an end is cut by half the thickness of the perpendicular recovered wall whose centreline lands on it. Third, since #274 (RE-29) a candidate must additionally be NAMED in this record's counted reference list at +0x88, and is tested for reach against its own cut-back run rather than its recorded one. All inputs are recorded bounding boxes and nothing is fitted; candidates disagreeing about their thickness decline the whole element, and a trim that would collapse the run declines it too. Measured against Revit's own export (world axis-aligned bounding box, max of the two corner deltas, tolerance 1e-3 ft; RE-26 used IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, RE-29 used tools/re/ifc_world_aabb.py, which reproduces every RE-26 table exactly): 336 of 360 walls exact at RE-26 and 351 of 360 after RE-29, up from 27 before either; correct wall ends 689 -> 703 (membership) -> 711 of 720; mean residual 0.2701 -> 0.0220 -> 0.0081 ft. Per element 15 walls improve, 345 are unchanged and 0 regress. Status is partial, not verified, for two reasons. The 9 ends still wrong are all over-trims at one side of a TRUE L CORNER - two walls whose runs both stop at the other's centreline with nothing continuing past, where Revit cuts exactly one of the pair. Two such corners exist on this file (one repeated on eight storeys) and no feature in the record orders the two sides: the survivor is the thicker wall once and an equal-thickness wall once, the x wall once and the y wall once, the higher ElementId once and the lower once, the longer run once and the shorter once, and the prologue flag words do not order them consistently either. The solver keeps cutting both rather than guessing, so the residual is recorded and pinned rather than hidden. And no witness compares body geometry, so this has not met the two-independent-witnesses bar in docs/verification-protocol.md. This models Revit's join cleanup on top of a carrier it does read; it does not read the per-pair butt/mitre decision itself. Emitted product counts, relations, storeys and the diagnostics sidecar are unchanged. This is not evidence for any other category or release.

capabilities.name: Column section and join-cut body from Revit 2024 element records
capabilities.evidence: partition_element_records::PartitionElementRecord::type_symbol_reference and element_record_column_cuts::{difference_box, column_cut_boxes} wired through partition_schema_mvp::column_instances_from_records; reports/element-framing/RE-26-world-coordinate-residuals.md and reports/element-framing/RE-29-join-reference-list.md; gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_column_type_symbol_join (256 of 256 columns join to symbol 5755) and ::core_interior_2024_column_join_cut_plan_extents (the cut plan rectangles reproduce Revit's own body-extent histogram exactly: 176 x 2.0x2.0, 38 x 1.6667x1.6667, 20 x 1.75x1.6667, 18 x 1.4167x1.6667, 4 x 2.0x1.6667 ft), plus the unit gates in src/partition_element_records.rs and src/element_record_column_cuts.rs
capabilities.user_impact: A recovered column's profile is the one its family type declares, and its body is the prism minus the walls that cut it, so a column that Revit trims where a wall passes through it no longer exports oversized.
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Columns, -2000100), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. The type join is exact and byte-anchored: the last slot before the record's own ElementId in the counted reference list at +0x88 that is itself an OST_Columns record carrying placement kind 0xffff8000 (the type-symbol envelopes of RE-21 section 5). All 256 exported columns have exactly one candidate before their own id and it is 5755 (Column_Sqaure : 24 inch x 24 inch), which is the IfcColumnType.Tag Revit's own export writes for every one of them. The join ships with a fail-closed guard: the type section and the instance plan envelope must agree to 1e-6 ft or the join is dropped and the element keeps its envelope with ProfileResolved false. RE-26 left the body residual open - 176 of 256 columns were world-exact and the 80 that were not had a body Revit cuts inset from the full prism, which no section can produce. #274 (RE-29) closes it from the same +0x88 list: a column record names the walls that cut it, and the exported body is the record prism minus the UNTRIMMED record prisms of those walls - 256 of 256 exact at a worst residual of 9.4e-13 ft and a mean of 0.0000 ft, against 176 of 256 at 0.5833 ft / 0.1217 ft before, with 80 improved, 176 unchanged and 0 regressed. Substituting the join-trimmed wall runs scores 190 of 256, so a wall runs its full recorded length into a column it cuts. element_record_column_cuts::difference_box is fail-closed: it answers only when the surviving material fills its own bounding box exactly by volume, which on this file is true on every one of the 80 columns whose box shrinks and false on every one of the 69 interior slots, Ls and crosses, so a decline never emits material Revit removed and the emitted solid is never larger on any axis than what Revit kept. Status stays partial because the section is still only the symbol's bounding box and the cut is still a box difference rather than a recovered solid, and because no witness compares profile or body geometry - the OctetProof claimed surface scores counts and relations, not shapes. The one emitted count that moves is IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE 9231 -> 9311, the new JoinCutWallCount provenance row per cut column; BodySource becomes partition_element_record_join_cut on those columns. This is not evidence for any other category or release.

capabilities.name: Wall type record and the wall to IfcWallType join from Revit 2024 element records
capabilities.evidence: rvt::partition_type_records::{type_definition_ids, unique_type_reference}; reports/element-framing/RE-28-wall-type-records.md; gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_wall_type_record_join and ::core_interior_2024_material_record_family plus the unit gates in src/partition_type_records.rs; recorded in the walls and materials rows of both magnetar count manifests (tests/fixtures/project-counts/2024-core-interior-slim.json and 2024-core-interior.json)
capabilities.user_impact: None yet in the exported file. The join is available to library callers; it is deliberately not written onto the emitted wall, because adding a property would move the committed witness observation hashes.
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Walls, -2000011), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. A Revit wall TYPE has the bbox-less RE-24 record shape - the 88-byte prologue and the ff ff ff ff ab 05 marker at +0x50 with no bounding box - and a third value of the RE-21 placement-kind word at +0x42, 0xffff8080, alongside a counted slot list starting at +0x56 that names the record's own id. Eight OST_Walls records carry that shape on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt (ids 1710, 1711, 3897, 11356, 17328, 17337, 17339, 17341); Revit's own export writes four of them as IfcWallType and never places the other four, so the record set is a superset by construction and is NOT used as an IfcWallType recovery on its own. What is measured is the join: every one of the 360 exported wall instance records names exactly ONE of the eight in its +0x88 reference list - never zero, never two - and it is the IfcWallType.Tag the export assigns, 360 of 360 with no wrong answer and no miss, against 356 of 360 for RE-26's positional references[1] read. The recovered distribution equals the export's own IfcRelDefinesByType distribution exactly: 129 / 127 / 100 / 4. That also settles RE-26 section 9 and #240: the four 18-inch Basement walls read 1851 at references[1] because the list is ascending and 1851 (a record of category -2009014, not a wall type) sorts first - an index artifact, not a second id space or a type-graph indirection. Status is partial, not verified, for two reasons. First, nothing is emitted: no IFC entity, property or relation changes, tests/fixtures/synthetic-project.ifc is byte-identical, every committed OctetProof observation and verdict is untouched, and no count in either manifest moves. Second, no witness scores a wall-to-type relation, so this has not met the two-independent-witnesses bar in docs/verification-protocol.md. Separately and explicitly NOT claimed: compound layer thicknesses. A 128 KiB sweep centred on each of the four exported wall-type records finds 0 runs of consecutive f64 summing to that type's nominal width, and the paired reference export is a ReferenceView_V1.2 file carrying 0 IfcMaterialLayerSet, 0 IfcMaterialLayer and 0 IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage, so #88's layer-thickness criterion has no oracle on this artifact and can be neither met nor refuted here. No layer set is emitted and none is invented. This is not evidence for any other category or release.

capabilities.name: Revit 2024 Level names and elevations from partition Level records
capabilities.evidence: partition_level_records::scan_partition_levels + ifc::apply_partition_level_storeys; on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt the fifteen standalone OST_Levels records each own exactly one name/elevation parameter block, and all fifteen (name, elevation) pairs equal an IfcBuildingStorey Name/Elevation in both paired Revit exports - Basement 2 -40, Basement 1 -20, Level 1 0, Mez 1-2 15, Level 3/4/4 - Wall Layouts 1/2/3 at 31/46/61, Level 6..13 at 76/91/106/121/136/151/166/185.5 ft, no wrong elevation, no missing storey, no extra storey; tests/fixtures/project-counts/2024-core-interior*.json gate diagnostics.exported.storey_count at 15 tolerance 0 with levels status known, and both OctetProof verdicts carry entity_counts.IFCBUILDINGSTOREY and storeys.IFCBUILDINGSTOREY inside the claimed surface, where rvt-rs, IfcOpenShell 0.8.5 and IFClite 7.1.1 emit byte-identical fifteen-pair sets
capabilities.notes: Scope is one BuiltInCategory (OST_Levels), one release band (Revit 2024) and one recorded edge. A Level record carries the same 88-byte element-record prologue but no bounding box - it ends at +0x56 where a column record's bbox would start - so it is decoded by its own reader, anchored on the 6-byte ff ff ff ff ab 05 marker at +0x50 and gated on the leading ElementId being declared in Global/ElemTable. Which of the 75 OST_Levels records on this file is a Level element is the same #211 instance test used for walls and columns: no container reference at +0x32, placement kind 0xffffef7f at +0x42. That selects exactly 15. The name and elevation come from a parameter block whose owner slot is a u64 at value-0x47, followed by a 56-byte 0xff sentinel run, three zero bytes and the u32 UTF-16 length; the elevation is an f64 in feet 55 bytes past an 8-byte marker (05 00 00 00 48 02 00 00) searched forward from the end of the name, repeated 153 bytes later, and both copies must agree. The run between name and marker is variable (347 bytes for fourteen levels, 363 for Basement 2), which is why the marker is searched rather than assumed. Fail-closed twice: a level with no accepted block emits nothing, and the whole recovery is discarded unless every Level record owns exactly one block and no two levels share an elevation - a partial recovery is never emitted as a smaller building. The names are asserted because the file states the pairing (the block is keyed by the Level's own ElementId), not because they were joined by rank; #213's rank join is what this replaces. Recovering a Level's own ElementId is not the same as binding a Floor or a Room to one - level-elementid-storey-bind stays unsupported (#86 / RE-20). Storey containment measured on this storey set was 801 of 872 elements when it landed and is 853 of 872 after #219 / RE-27 bound the record-named Level; see record-level-reference-storey-bind. This is not evidence for any other category or release.
capabilities.user_impact: A Revit 2024 project exports with its real Level names and heights - Basement 2, Mez 1-2, Level 13 - instead of elevation-derived labels, and every storey the project has is present rather than only the ones with a column standing on them.

capabilities.name: Storey elevations and containment from Revit 2024 element-record bounding boxes
capabilities.evidence: element_record_storeys + ifc::apply_element_record_storeys; on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt the 256 OST_Columns records carry 11 distinct base elevations (0, 31, 46, 61, 76, 91, 106, 121, 136, 151, 166 ft) and all 11 equal an IfcBuildingStorey.Elevation in the paired Revit export, measured with IfcOpenShell 0.8.5; IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure 1 -> 11 with 794 of 872 elements bound after #212 (all 256 columns, all 132 doors, 355 of 360 walls, 51 of 100 record-backed plates), measured on the commit before #218 replaced the storey source
capabilities.notes: Elevations only. The join is elevation equality within 1e-3 ft and fails closed on both a miss and an ambiguity, and the storey set is derived this way only when the recovered Level rows carry no elevation of their own. It does not recover which named Level sits at an elevation - 12 name candidates against 11 measured elevations is not a pairing, and a rank join mislabels (Level 6 at 91 ft where the export puts Level 7) - so storeys are labelled 'Elevation N ft'. Level ElementId binding stays unsupported (#86 / RE-20). Scope is Revit 2024 partition element records: only OST_Columns *supplies* elevations, a restriction measured in RE-21 (doors 11 of 11 also land on storeys, walls 12 of 13 - they add -40 ft at the cost of one non-storey elevation - and windows 0 of 6, because a window base is a sill height). Every record-bodied element *binds* to the column-derived set by exact match. The export's other four storeys (-40, -20, 15, 185.5 ft) carry no column record and are not recovered. Re-measured in RE-22 (#212): plates bind by their record TOP face, not their base — Revit hangs a floor below the level that hosts it, so 0 of 40 distinct slab base elevations is a storey elevation while 51 of 100 plates have a top that equals one, every one of them the storey Revit's own export assigns. Slab records are still not an elevation *source*: their 26 distinct top elevations would add -40 ft and 185.5 ft (two of the four storeys this recovery misses) at the cost of 13 values that are not storey elevations, each 0.1667 ft below a real one, so STOREY_ELEVATION_SOURCE_TYPES stays IFCCOLUMN alone. Superseded as the primary storey source on 2026-08-30 by record-level-storeys (#218, RE-24), which reads the Revit Level elements themselves and recovers all 15 storeys with their names; this path now runs only when no Level records are recoverable, and the binding half it contributes is unchanged.
capabilities.user_impact: Columns from a Revit 2024 project land in storeys at their real elevations instead of all defaulting to the first storey; the storeys are labelled by elevation, not by Revit Level name.

capabilities.name: Storey containment from the Level ElementId a Revit 2024 element record names
capabilities.evidence: element_record_level_refs::unique_level_reference + ifc::apply_record_level_reference_storeys; on 2024_Core_Interior.rvt the counted reference list at +0x88 names exactly one of the fifteen recovered Levels on 121 of 146 OST_Floors, 267 of 320 OST_Doors, 206 of 1487 OST_Walls, 6 of 7 OST_Windows and 1 of 2 OST_BuildingPad placed instances, and on 0 of 463 OST_Columns, which all name two; over the 537 elements the #212 / #213 elevation join also answers, the two joins agree 537 of 537 with 0 disagreements; emitted storey containment 801 -> 853 of 872 building elements (IFCSLAB 44 -> 80 of 80, IFCSHADINGDEVICE 10 -> 20 of 20, IFCWINDOW 0 -> 6 of 6), gated by tests/iter_elements_typed.rs::core_interior_2024_storey_containment_is_evidence_backed
capabilities.notes: Scope is Revit 2024 partition element records, and the join is stated by the file rather than inferred: the host Level is a plain ElementId slot in the same counted list RE-23 reads for a door's host wall. Fail-closed three times over. A record that names no Level, or two or more, resolves to nothing and keeps whatever the elevation join gives it - a Revit column or wall carries a base and a top constraint and both are in the list, with nothing in the bytes saying which slot is which, so 344 of 344 OST_Columns records and 432 of 638 OST_Walls records that name a Level at all are declined. The id set the uniqueness test runs against is deliberately the broader one (every standalone OST_Levels record, not only the fifteen the RE-24 name / elevation recovery validates), so a Level the full recovery would drop still makes a record ambiguous; the binding half then uses only the validated fifteen, and a named Level outside them binds nothing. This is NOT the #86 / RE-20 typed level bind: level_bind.rs binds a typed Floor or Room through an m_level_id schema field, that field is still unrecovered, and level-elementid-storey-bind stays unsupported. On a release or file where partition_element_records or partition_level_records decline, the level-id set is empty and nothing changes - verified unchanged on the 2023 Einhoven sample. The reference side was NOT MEASURED: the paired Revit export is not in this checkout, so none of the 853 is scored against Revit's own IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure. Elements with no recovered storey are now contained in the IfcBuilding rather than in storey[0], which had put 71 elements - some at 185 ft - into Basement 2 at -40 ft. See reports/element-framing/RE-27-level-reference-storey-bind.md.
capabilities.user_impact: A Revit 2024 project exports with its floor plates, shading plates and windows on the Revit Level that hosts them, instead of unplaced because a plate hangs two inches below its level and a window sits at its sill height above it; and an element whose storey is unknown is visibly unplaced in the building rather than silently filed under the lowest basement.
